page: Alibaba Cloud ecs.se1.4xlarge is a memory-optimized instance powered by the KVM hypervisor. It features 16 dedicated physical cores on an x86_64 architecture, utilizing an Intel Xeon 8269CY processor running at 2.5 GHz. The system is configured with 128.0 GB of RAM, yielding a high resource density of 8.0 GB of memory per core. It does not include local storage or dedicated GPU hardware, and it operates with a baseline network bandwidth of 3 Gbps.

Benchmark data reveals a clear distinction between single-core and multi-core capabilities. Single-core performance is weak, with stress-ng single-core and Geekbench single-core scores falling into the bottom 25%, and single-threaded gzip compression ranking in the bottom 10%. Conversely, multi-core execution is more robust, achieving average tier results in stress-ng multi-core, Geekbench multi-core, and multi-threaded bzip3 decompression. Memory bandwidth benchmarks for both cached and uncached large blocks also register in the average tier, though the Passmark memory score is weak.

Given the 8:1 memory-to-vCPU ratio and average multi-core performance, this instance is structured for memory-intensive workloads that do not demand high single-thread CPU speed. It is appropriate for database operations, caching layers like Redis, and moderate multi-threaded processing. From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the dedicated core allocation and high memory density provide stable resource availability, though the lack of local storage requires external block storage integration, which may impact overall I/O-bound cost-to-performance ratios.
